Do you need a permit for a steel building? What to ask your county

4 min readUpdated 2026-11-16

The honest answer is: it depends on where you build. Permit rules for accessory buildings are set by your county or city, not by the building company. Here is what to ask before you order.

Questions to ask your county or city

  • Do I need a permit for a building this size?
  • What are the setback rules from property lines, roads and septic?
  • Do you require engineered, stamped plans? Which wind and snow loads?
  • Is a foundation inspection required before the building goes up?
  • Are there size limits on accessory buildings on my lot?

Check the private rules too

HOA covenants and deed restrictions can limit size, height, color and placement even when the county says yes.

Call 811 before anyone digs

Utility lines need to be marked before slab work or anchors go in. It is free, and it is the law in most places.

What engineered plans cover

Plans for your site should state the wind and snow loads they are designed for and include foundation details. Ask your building company whether plans are included, and whether they are designed for your exact ZIP code.

We can tell you what to ask for your area. Call or text us with your ZIP.
